note: Derived from the repository only. This app is a single-user macOS desktop application; most of a web matrix does not apply and is marked NOT_APPLICABLE rather than guessed.

os.testedOn: macOS 24.4.0 (Darwin), the only machine in evidence

architecture.builtBinaries: x86_64 (both the Swift launcher and the bundled node are Mach-O x86_64)
architecture.appleSilicon: Runs under Rosetta only. scripts/bundle-app selects the CPython triple from `uname -m`, so a build ON an arm64 Mac would produce an arm64 bundle, but no universal binary is produced and none has been tested. DOCKET B4.
architecture.risk: A bundle built on x86_64 and handed to an arm64 Mac carries an x86_64 node and an x86_64 CPython.

browser.runtime: WKWebView inside the native wrapper (native/main.swift). There is no browser support matrix — the app ships its own web view.
browser.alsoReachable: Any browser at http://127.0.0.1:4737 while the server runs; the launch-snipai.command path opens the default browser. Untested in Safari/Chrome/Firefox as products.
browser.knownWebViewDifference: Backspace was historically treated as Back by the web view; the review screen calls preventDefault unconditionally on Delete/Backspace because of it.

display.openBehaviour: always centered on the PRIMARY display (NSScreen.screens.first), deliberately not the last frame
display.responsive: UNKNOWN below 900x600 — the native window cannot go smaller, but a browser can. No mobile layout exists.

hardware.cpu: Whisper and ffmpeg are the load. lib/pipeline.ts runs children at low priority and sets OMP_NUM_THREADS/MKL_NUM_THREADS; the tools honour SNIPAI_THREADS.
hardware.ram: A 700MB upload measured 149MB peak RSS after the streaming fix (2169MB before). 4K H.264 encode is the other pressure. The host machine went into swap and rebooted under the pre-fix buffering.
hardware.disk: Library measured at 8.8GB for two projects. Build caches: .next 136M, .build-cache 543M, node_modules 250M, .venv 433M, SnipAi.app 666M.

media.mismatch: The reference uploader accepts a NARROWER set than the project importer (no .avi/.mkv). Worth a test.
media.referenceSizeCap: 600MB (app/api/references/route.ts). The project importer has NO size cap.
media.testedFootage: 4K HEVC .MOV from an iPhone, 30fps, portrait 2160x3840, 1.7-1.8GB, ~9-11 minutes
media.renderOutput: H.264 yuv420p + AAC 192k, source resolution, faststart. The auto pipeline instead renders from the 720p proxy.

network.required: NONE for the core product. Nothing is fetched at runtime; the server is loopback-only.
network.offline: Fully functional offline. This is a genuine strength and should be asserted by the gauntlet, not assumed.

notApplicable: screen readers on web (no a11y work has been done — see risks)
